title: The Newsroom Kill Order
logline: An investigative journalist writing for an independent station broadsheet discovers that their publisher took secret debt forgiveness from a shipping cartel to suppress an expose on migrant dock worker casualties.

roles.description: Tenacious station reporter working out of a crowded print shop; underslept, proud, and determined to publish.
Owner of the independent station gazette; weary, deeply indebted, and protecting the press from bankruptcy.
Former shift boss at the freight intake berths; crippled by an unlogged crane collapse and seeking justice.
A clattering newsroom and printing press module wedged between freight concourses.
The private cargo logistics syndicate that operates the station's heavy unloading slips.

public_situation: The independent station gazette delays its scheduled morning edition, posting a brief notice citing printing press mechanical overhauls.
private_truth: The publisher accepted complete debt cancellation from {role:freight_consortium} in exchange for shredding a front-page investigation into forty unrecorded dockworker fatalities.

beats.public_change: Freight security personnel linger outside {role:press_office_dock} observing visitors entering the newspaper offices.

missions.reason: She pays an outside pilot to collect an encrypted memory plate from an industrial clinic dock containing corroborated medical morgue manifests.
missions.private_fact: Her publisher ordered her off the freight story two hours before the press run and locked the composition room terminal.

beats.public_change: {role:broadsheet_publisher} announces a new sponsor agreement with the cargo syndicate, replacing the lead edition with an advertorial feature.

missions.reason: He pays the pilot to scan the publisher's escrow terminal to verify that the newsroom's commercial loan mortgages were stamped paid by the freight syndicate's bank.
missions.private_fact: His younger brother's fatal gantry crushing was logged in corporate records as an off-duty respiratory accident.

beats.public_change: Night crews assemble at {role:press_office_dock} as the publisher prepares to load the sterilized edition onto distribution rollers.

missions.reason: She asks the pilot to courier manual metal printing plates of the true investigation to the press floor before corporate enforcers confiscate them.
missions.private_fact: If the publisher burns the plates, she intends to resign and smuggle hand-printed pamphlets through the residential rings.

player_choice.prompt: Holding the corroborated fatality records and the proof of the publisher's secret debt relief, the pilot must decide whether to force the true edition onto the press, broker a quiet medical settlement, or accept the publisher's buyout.

options.label: Force the original casualty expose onto the press rollers to trigger a public station reckoning
Use the plates to force the publisher and consortium into an anonymous compensation trust for the victims' families
Surrender the plates to the publisher to collect a quiet cut of the cartel's payoff

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot forces the casualty expose onto the printing press.
resolutions.summary: The newspaper hits the stands. Outraged dockers strike, {role:freight_consortium} faces municipal manslaughter charges, and {role:broadsheet_publisher} resigns.

consequences.public_summary: A pilot forced an independent newspaper to publish evidence of corporate dockworker deaths.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot brokers a quiet private endowment for the families.
resolutions.summary: {role:freight_consortium} establishes a private disability trust. The expose is suppressed, but {role:dock_labour_witness} secures lifetime support for surviving families.

consequences.public_summary: A pilot forced a freight cartel to quietly pay lifetime settlements to injured dockworkers.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot sells the plates to the publisher or abandons the print run.
resolutions.summary: The sanitized edition prints smoothly. {role:broadsheet_publisher} pockets full debt cancellation, while {role:investigative_reporter} is blacklisted across the sector.

consequences.public_summary: A pilot assisted a compromised publisher in destroying an investigative report into dock fatalities.

loose_threads.detail: A commercial newsprint supplier registered an unlisted third-party debt cancellation voucher for the newspaper's rolling press machinery.
The cargo crane maintenance certificate bears an illegible inspector stamp dating from three weeks before the structural failure.

radio_hooks: Station broadsheet delays morning print run citing technical recalibration.
Cargo logistics guild commends dock safety records during annual municipal review.
Warehouse workers voice frustration over unexplained loading bay slowdowns.

voice_direction.investigative_reporter: Fast-paced, razor-sharp, and speaks with relentless journalistic intensity. Never uses corporate or bureaucratic euphemisms.
voice_direction.broadsheet_publisher: Weary, defensive, and speaks in long, rationalizing sentences. Constantly justifies moral compromises as business necessities.
voice_direction.dock_labour_witness: Slow, raspy, and pauses frequently as if struggling with physical discomfort. Speaks with heavy, unyielding moral conviction.
